title: Divisibility of Non-Invertible Quantum Dynamics in the Heisenberg Picture
abstract: We study divisibility of finite-dimensional quantum dynamics in the Heisenberg picture when the dynamical maps need not be invertible. Heisenberg divisible dynamics determines unique reduced propagators on the accessible operator systems, and Heisenberg CP-divisibility is shown to be equivalent to an operator-norm monotonicity. Although each reduced propagator admits a unital completely positive extension, independently chosen extensions need not satisfy a composition law. Generalized inverses restore this law algebraically, but do not, in general, preserve complete positivity. We characterize the resulting obstruction and give a sufficient construction based on unital completely positive projections onto the accessible operator systems. It is shown that for qubit dynamics Heisenberg CP-divisibility always guarantees a completely positive generalized-inverse propagator. Finally, we analyze time-local generators at singular times and identify the associated gauge freedom on dynamically inaccessible directions.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes the concept of quantum dynamical divisibility, especially when the evolution maps are not invertible. It establishes that Heisenberg CP-divisibility is equivalent to an operator-norm monotonicity condition, providing necessary and sufficient mathematical criteria for consistent time evolution. The findings are important for understanding the mathematical structure of open quantum systems beyond the standard unitary or trace-preserving assumptions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical conditions for the divisibility of quantum dynamics, particularly when the underlying dynamical maps are non-invertible in the Heisenberg picture.
main_result: Heisenberg CP-divisibility is characterized by an operator-norm monotonicity condition, and for qubit dynamics, this guarantees a completely positive generalized-inverse propagator.
method: The authors use functional analysis, comparing standard divisibility definitions with necessary kernel inclusion conditions for non-invertible maps, and employing generalized inverse constructions.
model_or_system: The study concerns general finite-dimensional quantum dynamics on matrix algebras ($M_d$), represented by dynamical maps ($\Lambda_t$ in Schrödinger picture, $\Lambda_t^*$ in Heisenberg picture).
key_observables: Divisibility (existence of intermediate maps), CP-divisibility, operator-norm monotonicity, and the structure of reduced propagators on accessible operator systems.
important_parameters: The dimension of the system ($d$), and the time evolution parameter $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often proceeds by assuming the existence of reduced propagators or by analyzing the failure of these assumptions when maps are non-invertible.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the failure of standard divisibility definitions for non-invertible maps, then characterizing Heisenberg CP-divisibility via norm inequalities and kernel inclusions, and finally developing gauge-invariant formulations to handle singular time generators.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze the consistency of quantum evolution when the system dynamics are non-unitary or non-invertible, which is crucial for modeling open quantum systems.
